subject: Quantitative Reasoning
introduction: Speed, time and distance are governed by the fundamental relation: Distance = Speed × Time. Mastering this requires handling unit conversions (km/h ↔ m/s), relative speed for objects moving toward or away from each other, and average speed calculations.

key_formulas.name: Relative speed (approaching)
key_formulas.formula: S_{rel} = S_1 + S_2 \text{ (moving toward each other)}

key_formulas.name: Train crossing
key_formulas.formula: \text{Time} = \frac{\text{Length of train + Length of object}}{\text{Speed of train}}

tips_and_tricks: Always check units — convert everything to same unit before computing.
Average speed ≠ arithmetic mean of speeds. Use Total Distance / Total Time.
Two objects toward each other: closing speed = S1+S2. Time to meet = D/(S1+S2).
Two objects same direction: relative speed = |S1-S2|. Time to meet/overtake = D/(S1~S2).
Train crossing a person: time = train length / train speed.
Train crossing a platform: time = (train length + platform length) / train speed.
If equal distances at different speeds: avg speed = 2S1S2/(S1+S2) (harmonic mean).

questions.subject: Quantitative Reasoning
questions.question_text: A man walks at 5km/h and jogs at 10km/h. He covers 20km total, spending equal time on each. Find total time.
questions.explanation:
Let time = t each. Distance=5t+10t=15t=20 → t=4/3h.
Total time=2×4/3=8/3h=**2h 40min** ✓
hints: Let equal time=t. Total distance=15t=20 → t=4/3.

questions.subject: Quantitative Reasoning
questions.question_text: Rudi leaves A at 8:00am at 40km/h. Siti leaves A at 9:00am at 60km/h in the same direction. When does Siti overtake Rudi?
questions.explanation: By 9am, Rudi is 40km ahead. Relative speed=20km/h. Time to overtake=40/20=2h. Siti started at 9am → overtakes at **11:00am** ✓

questions.subject: Quantitative Reasoning
questions.question_text: Two trees 480m apart. A ant goes from Tree A at 2m/s. B ant from Tree B at 4m/s. Toward each other. Where do they meet from Tree A?
questions.explanation: Relative speed=6m/s. Meet time=480/6=80s. A traveled=2×80=**160m** from Tree A ✓

questions.subject: Quantitative Reasoning
questions.question_text: A and B run a 1km race. A beats B by 100m or 20 seconds. Find B's speed.
questions.explanation: B runs 900m in time A runs 1000m. Also B takes 20 more seconds. B's speed=900m÷?. Since beat by 100m=20s: B covers 100m in 20s → speed=100/20=**5 m/s** ✓
hints: B is 100m behind when A finishes.

questions.subject: Quantitative Reasoning
questions.question_text: A car starts at 60km/h. Due to traffic, it reduces speed by 10km/h every 30 minutes. How far does it travel in 1.5 hours?
questions.explanation:
Segment 1 (0-0.5h at 60km/h): 30km.
Segment 2 (0.5-1h at 50km/h): 25km.
Segment 3 (1-1.5h at 40km/h): 20km.
Total: 30+25+20=**75km**. So answer B=75km. Let me fix option A to 75km.

questions.subject: Quantitative Reasoning
questions.question_text: A is 30km before B on a road. Both head in the same direction. A: 60km/h, B: 40km/h. When is the gap 50km?
questions.explanation: Initial gap=30km. A is ahead. A moves faster → gap INCREASES at relative speed=20km/h. Additional gap needed=50-30=20km. Time=20/20=**1 hour** ✓
hints: A is 30km ahead, moving faster. Gap increases at 60-40=20 km/h.
Need gap to grow from 30→50km: need 20 more km.
